page: Microsoft Azure D2als_v7 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the Dalsv7 family. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core of an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz. The processor includes 32 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1d cache. It is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPUs, but it is premium storage capable.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The high-frequency AMD processor delivers top-tier single-core performance, as demonstrated by stress-ng single-core CPU tests, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression. However, due to its low core count, multi-core performance is weak, placing in the bottom 25% for stress-ng multi-core tests, PassMark CPU scores, and PassMark database operations. Memory bandwidth for large blocks is average, while small-block cached read-only memory bandwidth is weak.

The primary tradeoff of the D2als_v7 is its low memory-to-CPU ratio and lack of local storage. With only 4.0 GB of RAM, it is a low-memory configuration that limits its capability for memory-intensive workloads. Qualitatively, it offers a cost-efficient entry point for compute-focused tasks that require high single-thread performance without the overhead of large memory capacities.

This server is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded applications, basic web serving, simple background workers, and small-scale text processing or compression tasks. It is not recommended for database hosting, multi-threaded high-performance computing, or memory-heavy applications.
